t: The correct order of decreasing second ionisation enthalpy of Ti (22), V (23), Cr (24) and Mn (25) is-
s:
Electronic configuration of the given elements are
Mn→1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶3d⁵4s²
Cr→1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶3d⁵4s¹
Ti→1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶3d²4s²
V→1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶3d³4s²
In general, ionization potential ( both 1st and 2nd ) increases form left to right across the period due to increase in effective nuclear charge. On this basis, the second IP values should exhibit the trend :
Mn > Cr > V > Ti
But the actual observed order is :
Cr > Mn > V > Ti
Practically, only chromium is exceptional and rest others show the normal trend. This exceptional behaviour of chromium is due to the stable configuration ( 3d5 ) that it achieves after the loss of first electron.

t: The Irving-Williams order regarding the stability of the complexes of bivalent metal of the first transition series is
s:
The Irving-Williams series describes the relative stabilities of complexes formed by high-spin bivalent metal ions of the first transition series.
The stability of these complexes generally increases across the period from Mn²⁺ to Cu²⁺ and then decreases for Zn²⁺.
This trend is primarily due to the steady decrease in the ionic radius and the corresponding increase in effective nuclear charge, which leads to stronger metal-ligand electrostatic interactions. Furthermore, the Ligand Field Stabilization Energy (LFSE) contributes to this trend.
The stability reaches a maximum at Cu²⁺ (d⁹) due to significant extra stabilization from Jahn-Teller distortion. The stability drops for Zn²⁺ (d¹⁰) because it has a completely filled d-subshell, resulting in zero LFSE.
Therefore, the observed Irving-Williams order is Mn<Fe<Co<Ni<Cu>Zn. .
o: Mn < Fe < Co < Ni < Cu > Zn
Mn > Fe > Co > Ni > Cu > Zn
Mn < Fe < Co > Ni > Cu > Zn
Mn > Fe > Co < Ni < Cu < Zn
